title: Prompt Chaining
brief: Marketing wants three pieces of launch copy. Each brief has 4 hard rules: a word limit, the discount code SPRING20, the legal line, and no banned words. One big prompt gets all four right only about half the time. Get at least 85% of pieces right, in 6 turns or fewer on average.

data.systemPrompt: Write launch copy that follows every rule in the brief.
Write launch copy that follows every rule in the brief.

data.name: write_outline
data.description: Step 1. Writes a bullet outline of the copy from the brief: headline, 3 points, call to action.

data.name: check_outline
data.description: Gate. Checks the outline in code against the brief rules (code present, legal line, banned words) and lists any misses.

data.name: write_copy
data.description: Step 3. Writes the final copy from a checked outline, within the word limit.

tasks.label: Launch email
tasks.prompt: Write the spring launch email for Ledgerly. Max 150 words. Must include code SPRING20 and the line 'Offer ends April 30. Terms apply.' Never say 'revolutionary' or 'free'.

tasks.label: Landing page hero
tasks.prompt: Write the landing page hero for the Ledgerly spring sale. Max 40 words. Must include SPRING20 and 'Terms apply.' No exclamation marks.

tasks.label: App store blurb
tasks.prompt: Write the app store 'What's new' text for Ledgerly 4.0. Max 80 words. Mention the SPRING20 code and the legal line. Do not compare to competitors by name.

one_ok.text: Here is your copy: 'Close your books in half the time. Use SPRING20 for 20% off your first year. Offer ends April 30. Terms apply.' (138 words, all four rules met)

one_miss.text: Here is your copy: 'Meet the revolutionary new Ledgerly! Close your books in half the time...' (212 words, no SPRING20 code, legal line missing)

outline.text: write_outline(brief) → headline, 3 points, CTA with SPRING20

gate_fix.text: Gate flagged a miss: the outline has no legal line. Adding 'Offer ends April 30. Terms apply.' to the CTA before writing.

done.text: Final copy attached. Gate passed: 141 words, SPRING20 present, legal line present, no banned words.

done_miss.text: Final copy attached. (The unchecked outline had no legal line, so the copy has none either.)

modifiers.note: A bigger model helps a little, but four rules in one pass still slip.
With chain steps wired, the model follows them in order.
About 1 outline in 4 fails the gate and gets fixed before any copy is written.
Without the gate, a bad outline flows straight into the final copy.

goals.label: At least 85% of pieces meet every rule

hints: Read a failing transcript. Which rule slipped? Would a bigger model fix it? Try large and see.
Split the job into steps that each do one thing: outline, then copy. Something has to run the steps, so add a Loop.
Add three tools on the loop: write_outline, check_outline (the gate) and write_copy. Without check_outline, a bad outline still flows into the copy.
explain: A chain trades one hard call for several easy ones, and the gate between them is plain code that catches a miss before it spreads. You pay for more calls; you get copy that follows the brief.
